assertions.title: Manage and calendar links from the captured email work

evidence.ics: guest-channels-and-crm/r2-manage-links/VAL-MSG-009-ics-responses.txt (GET /reservations/manage/calendar.ics -> 200, content-type text/calendar; DTSTART:20261018T230000Z, SUMMARY:Reservation at Erdman - Brakus)

assertions.notes: The manage link taken from the captured confirmation email (rsv-r2c-1@example.com, meta.messageKind=confirmation) was opened in the task's fresh agent-browser session before any login: document GET http://acme.menuza.test:3008/reserve/manage -> 200 (no 404); the view renders 'Hello, Rina', CONFIRMATION CODE 54F1K1PN, status badge 'Confirmed', WHEN Sunday, October 18, 2026, 7:00 PM, PARTY 2 guests, and the policy line 'You can cancel until Sun, Oct 18, 5:00 PM.' The page is anonymous — the site header still shows 'Sign in' and no login was performed before these checks. Tenant-api GET /reservations/manage -> 200 with the token. Calendar: the email's add-to-calendar link is a Google Calendar URL (not an .ics URL), so the .ics was checked through the contract path: GET /reservations/manage/calendar.ics with X-Reservation-Token -> 200, content-type text/calendar; charset=utf-8, content-disposition attachment; filename=reservation.ics, body SUMMARY 'Reservation at Erdman - Brakus' and DTSTART:20261018T230000Z = 2026-10-18 19:00 America/New_York, i.e. it matches the booking's first name/time/party (Rina, Sun Oct 18 7:00 PM, 2) and the venue/location (Downtown Flagship; LOCATION: Downtown Flagship). The manage page's own 'Add to calendar' button requested GET /reservations/manage/ics -> 200 with the same body. Token placement audited on the captured email HTML: the 104-char token occurs exactly once, inside the '#t=' fragment of 'http://acme.menuza.test:3008/reserve/manage#t=<manage token>'; no token in path or query (token-in-query=false, token-in-path=false), and no other href in the email carries a token.
assertions.limitations: The contract's evidence line names GET /reservations/manage/calendar.ics; the manage page's own button calls the alias /reservations/manage/ics. Both were exercised and both return 200 text/calendar with identical content. The same browser session was later used to log into the App in a second tab (per the parent's allowance); the manage-page checks were completed before that, the Sites origin never receives App cookies, and the flow was re-checked (console clean) after.

summary: Re-test after the manage-link fix (commit af7ffb5a, HEAD c043ba8f): both VAL-CROSS-011 and VAL-MSG-009 pass. The confirmation email and SMS now carry http://acme.menuza.test:3008/reserve/manage#t=<manage token> (the org's Sites origin, token only in the fragment), the manage page loads anonymously without 404, the .ics matches the booking (DTSTART 20261018T230000Z = 19:00 EDT), the guest modification to 20:00 emits a modification email and shows as a guest 'modified' event in kody's detail sheet, 19:00 frees on Sites, kody's cancel emits a cancellation_restaurant email and leaves the manage page in the cancelled state with no actions, and 20:00 is bookable again (second guest booked S87XKRY9). Console errors: none. Persisting observations: the operator cancel UI still takes no reason (cancel_reason NULL), and the manage page's add-to-calendar button uses /reservations/manage/ics (200 text/calendar) alongside the contract-named /reservations/manage/calendar.ics (also 200).
